newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RBA dividend to Australia govt halved to A$1.2 bln.
newsitem.headline: RBA dividend to Australia govt halved to A$1.2 bln.

text.p: The dividend paid by the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) to the government is expected to fall by over A$900 million in 1997/98 (July/June), due mainly to a stronger Australian dollar, budget papers show.
The RBA is expected to pay a dividend of A$1.200 billion in 1997/98, down 43.8 percent from a forecast A$2.136 billion in 1996/97, according to the budget papers released on Tuesday.

"The lower dividend estimate in 1997/98 reflects the effect on the RBA's 1996/97 earnings of expected asset valuation adjustments arising mainly form changes in exchange rates during 1996/97," the budget documents said.
"The stronger the Australian dollar, the lower is the value of the RBA's foreign exchange assets in Australian dollar terms," the papers said.
The RBA's underlying earnings were also expected to be reduced by changes in the structure of international and domestic interest rates.
Dividends from government communications business enterprises are expected to fall 16 percent to A$1.219 billion in 1997/98 from a forecast A$1.452 billion in 1996/97.

This is because the government's sale of one third of telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp will cut its entitlement to Telstra's dividend, although this will be partially offset by a special dividend payment of A$80 million from Australia Post.
Overall, total dividends and other payments to the government are projected at A$2.919 billion in 1997/98, a 28.9 percent fall on the A$4.104 billion expected in 1996/97.
